blocked.documented_effect: Describes rainwater-harvesting (runoff) agriculture, developed from ancient Negev runoff farms, as a way to produce food in arid zones where rainfall alone cannot support crops.
blocked.evidence_source: Bruins, H.J., Evenari, M. & Nessler, U. (1986). Rainwater-harvesting agriculture for food production in arid zones: the challenge of the African famine. Applied Geography 6(1): 13–32.
blocked.adaptation_notes: Catchment-to-cropped-area ratio must be sized to local rainfall and soil crusting; loess soils that crust generate runoff readily, sandy soils do not. Needs maintenance of bunds after every flood.
